analysis:
The PR changes only CI threat-review tooling. It touches no provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or billing code covered by the threat model (TB-002, TB-011 and related threats are unaffected).

threat-model-review.py (head 16-23, 31): the fixed 15-minute alarm becomes runtime_seconds(), with a default of 900 and a validated range of 60-3000s. The alarm is now set inside the try block, so an invalid value is caught by the generic handler (head 38-41), which writes diagnostics and a non-clean summary. Fail-closed behaviour is preserved, and the new message advises human review.

bedrock.py (head 46-55, 67-83, 87): adds a workload call policy. In workload mode the limit starts at 0 and rises via plan_calls up to a ceiling of at most 100, with one shared repair slot. Exceeding the ceiling sets workload_stopped, which raises BudgetStopped and blocks later calls through the stopped property. Fixed mode keeps the original bounded allowance. Invalid policy values are rejected. One gap: if callers never call plan_calls in workload mode, the limit stays 0, which blocks all calls (fails closed, not open). Callers of plan_calls (budget_runner) are not supplied, so planned-count correctness and cost bounds are unverified. This is a cost/availability concern for the CI pipeline, not product security.

Tests (head 743-760): the workflow is expected to pin base.sha without an env fallback, use a 60-minute timeout and a 3000s scan timeout, use the workload policy with 100 calls, and contain no workflow_dispatch, pr_number or review_depth in the review job. These assertions tighten the pull_request_target boundary. The workflow file itself is not supplied.

Open question: a 3000s alarm inside a 60-minute job leaves about 10 minutes to publish results, which looks consistent.

No product-security regression was identified.
